one_liner: Copper is a CRM with a public, read/write Developer API covering core sales records.

auth.notes: API keys are suitable for individual users; OAuth2.0 is preferred for partner integrations.

access.notes: API use is available during the free, 14-day trial. Only Admin users can generate API keys. Registering an OAuth application requires contacting Copper.

api.notes: The public reference covers core sales records and create, update and delete operations.

mcp.notes: A third-party connector is documented. Copper describes its own hosted MCP server as a forthcoming beta, not a presently available server.

verdict.rationale: The documented API is available during Copper’s free trial, but that path is time-limited and only Admin users can generate API keys. Registering an OAuth application requires contacting Copper.

evidence.quote: The Copper Developer API ("Dev API") provides a RESTful interface with JSON-formatted responses to access most Copper resources.
There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0. API Keys are suitable for individual users, while OAuth2.0 is the preferred approach for partner integrations.
Available on our trial, professional and business plan
Free 14-day trial No credit card required
Only Admin users are able to generate API Keys.
To register your application, contact us.
The Copper Developer API ("Dev API") provides a RESTful interface with JSON-formatted responses to access most Copper resources.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) allows you easily query your Copper data from within your favourite AI chatbot by simply connecting to our MCP server.
Copper is launching an official MCP server, built and hosted by Copper. The beta launches in November 2026.
Copper MCP server for AI agents and assistants

problems: Copper’s MCP page describes a forthcoming beta, not a presently available vendor-hosted server; its availability and eventual public pricing cannot be established from that page.
The help article establishes trial API availability but does not explicitly state the permissions assigned to a newly created trial account.
name: Copper

verification.note: The quote identifies API keys and OAuth2.0 and explicitly prefers OAuth2.0 for partner integrations.

The quotes establish API availability on a free 14-day trial and say only Admin users can generate API keys. OAuth application registration requires contact with Copper, but the trial API-key path supports the chosen level.
The public developer page documents a RESTful API accessing most Copper resources. The quotes do not specifically establish the note's claims about create, update, and delete operations.
A third-party page describes its Copper MCP server; Copper describes its official server as launching in a future beta.
The quote is from a Composio Copper toolkit page.

A documented, useful API is accessible through a time-limited self-serve trial, so buildable_with_caveats follows. With no trial-specific blocker value, other is reasonable; the OAuth registration requirement does not eliminate the trial API-key path.
